title: Zesty Fluffy Korean Semolina Kalguksu
description: A malty and fluffy Korean dish from the Gyeongsang region, featuring semolina flour and a flexitarian-friendly recipe, this kalguksu is a crowd-pleaser. It is cooked with binchotan-charcoal for a unique flavor.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine semolina flour, salt, and binchotan-charcoal powder, then gradually add in water to form a dough.
Knead the dough for 10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into 4 equal pieces and roll out each piece into a long rope.
Cut the rope into small pieces to form the kalguksu noodles.
In a large pot, bring a pot of water to a boil and cook the kalguksu noodles for 5 minutes, or until they float to the surface.
In a large skillet, heat sesame oil over medium heat and saute the diced zucchini, sliced mushrooms, and minced garlic until the vegetables are tender.
Add the cooked kalguksu noodles to the skillet and stir in soy sauce.
Season with salt to taste, then garnish with chopped green onions.
Serve the zesty fluffy Korean semolina kalguksu hot, straight from the skillet.
